Wocheneinkauf is a simple shared shopping list for families and flatmates. Create a list, share the link – everyone who opens it is in. No account, no tracking, no ads.

fdroid:at.techbee.jtx.name: jtx Board journals|notes|tasks
fdroid:at.techbee.jtx.summary: Keep track of journals, notes & tasks - iCalendar compliant and syncable with yo
fdroid:at.techbee.jtx.description:
Elevate the power of the iCalendar standard to the next level, use the potential of the combination of journals (VJournal), notes (VJournal) and tasks (VTodo) out of one app and use DAVx5 to synchronize your entries with a CalDAV-server of your choice!
 iCal standard compliant 
Using the iCal standard ensures compatibility and interoperability with other apps and services independent of a dedicated provider or infrastructure. Journals and Notes are compliant with the definition of the VJOURNAL component, Tasks are compliant with the VTODO component. You can also import and export your entries as .ics files.
 Combine journals, notes & tasks 
Instead of using separate apps for journals, notes & tasks you can use them out of one hand, combine and link them to each other, e.g. create meeting minutes and link your tasks to them.
 Sync with DAVx5 
Synchronize your entries with any compatible CalDAV server by using DAVx5. By using DAVx5 you are free to choose your preferred provider for CalDAV, you can even use your local server to store and synchronize your data.
Note: DAVx5 is an independent app and must be acquired separately.
 Open Source 
Your data can contain private and sensitive data by their nature. We believe that individuals and companies should be able to be in full control of their own data. This means the freedom to choose where and how the data are stored, and freedom in choice of software. That is why we chose DAVx5 as a Sync Adapter to synchronise your data between your phone and any compatible CalDAV-server. The source code for jtx Board is publically available - find out more on https://jtx.techbee.at !
 What does VJournal and VTodo mean? 
VJournal and VTodo are calendar components defined in the international standard RFC-5545, the Internet Calendaring and Scheduling Core Object Specification (iCalendar), see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5545 . This standard also defines the VEvent component, which is the standard definition for calendar event entries. jtx Board is using the VJournal component according to this iCalendar standard for journal entries and tasks. VJournals can have a defined start date, but they cannot have a duration or an end date. VJournals with a defined start date are considered journals entries in jtx Board, VJournals without start date are interpreted as notes. The VTodo component as defined in the iCalendar standard defines the technical specification of tasks, which can have a scheduled start, due and completed date as well as a progress and a completed status (amongst others).
The VEvent definition is widely used, the VTodo component also found some implementations in Apps, but the VJournal component remained in the dark almost not being implemented at all by other apps and services. With jtx Board we would like to revive the usage of this standard and empower it with the possibilities to link and combine VTodos with VJournals - and in the future also VEvents! :-)
Find out more on https://jtx.techbee.at

fdroid:com.quietgrid.app.name: Quiet Grid: Logic Puzzles
fdroid:com.quietgrid.app.summary: Sudoku, Nonogram, Minesweeper, Word Search & more. No ads, fully offline.
fdroid:com.quietgrid.app.description:
Quiet Grid is a calm collection of logic puzzles and word games: Sudoku, Nonogram, Takuzu, Minesweeper, Star Battle, Word Search, 2048 and more. No ads, no account, no internet. Everything stays on your device.
 A FRESH PUZZLE EVERY DAY 
Choose which games give you a new puzzle every day, in every difficulty. Share your result when you're done, and get an optional reminder if you haven't played yet.
 PUZZLES THAT PLAY FAIR 
 Four levels, Easy to Expert, graded by the logic each puzzle needs, not by how many squares are empty.
 Stuck? A hint shows you the next step.
 Challenger mode: solve as many puzzles as you can before the clock runs out.
 Build Mixes of your favorite games and difficulties and play them back to back.
 Track wins, streaks and scores for every game and difficulty, with a full history of every puzzle you play.
 LOGIC PUZZLES 
 Sudoku — Place digits 1–9 so every row, column and 3×3 box contains each digit once.
 Killer Sudoku — No starting digits: the sums in each dashed cage tell you what goes where.
 Mini Sudoku — Quick 4×4 and 6×6 Sudoku for a short break.
 Takuzu (Binairo) — Fill the grid with 0s and 1s. Equal counts, no three in a row, no identical rows.
 Nonogram (Hanjie) — Reveal a hidden picture using the number clues on each row and column.
 Minesweeper — Uncover every safe cell without hitting a mine.
 Star Battle — Place stars in every row, column and region, with no two touching.
 Animal Doku — One animal per row, column and colored region, never touching, not even diagonally.
 WORD GAMES 
 Word Search — Find hidden words in themed grids.
 Word Guess — Guess the hidden word in six tries.
 Guess by Numbers — Guess the word in ten tries; two numbers show how close you are.
 Theme Clear — Spell words from one theme until every letter is used.
 MEMORY, NUMBERS AND BLOCKS 
 Chimp Test — Tap the numbers in order before they disappear.
 Sequence Memory — Watch the pads light up, then tap the growing sequence back.
 2048 — Slide and merge tiles to reach 2048.
 Block Fill — Drag pieces onto the board and clear full rows and columns. Includes an Endless mode.
 Arrow Escape — Tap an arrow to send it off the board. It only gets out if nothing blocks its path.
 MAKE IT YOURS 
Seven color themes, including Pencil, a paper-like grayscale theme that works well for colorblind players. Play in English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese or Polish, and pick the language for word puzzles separately.
 CALM BY DESIGN 
Quiet Grid is made for calm, focused puzzle time. Hide the timer if you prefer. Daily puzzles, streaks and reminders only apply to the games you choose. Time pressure only when you start Challenger mode yourself.
 PRIVATE AND OPEN SOURCE 
No ads, no tracking, no account, and no internet permission. The only permission it asks for is notifications, for optional daily reminders. Open source under GPLv3.

fdroid:com.seca.messages.name: Seca Messages
fdroid:com.seca.messages.summary: Private SMS, and end-to-end encrypted messages between Seca phones
fdroid:com.seca.messages.description:
Ordinary texts, and end-to-end encrypted messages between Seca phones.
With Seca Link off, the app does not use the Internet at all. Turn it on and messages between two Seca phones travel encrypted with the Signal protocol, through public relays that see neither who writes nor what is written. No account, no server of ours.
One of three apps — Contacts, Phone and Messages — sharing one Material 3 Expressive design. Android 12 or newer, with or without Google, at its best on GrapheneOS. In English, French, German, Spanish and Polish.
 Seca Link: end-to-end encrypted 
 Between two Seca phones, messages travel encrypted with the Signal protocol (libsignal, post-quantum PQXDH), bypassing the carrier.
 No account, no Seca server: encrypted messages travel through public Nostr relays, which see neither who writes nor what is written.
 Two contacts connect through an invisible SMS; everything then goes over the Internet.
 Read receipts and typing indicator, each of which can be turned off.
 Safety number to compare, or to scan as a QR code.
 Encrypted photos and voice messages; the microphone is asked for only when you record one.
 Four public relays are set by default (relay.damus.io, nos.lol, relay.primal.net, nostr.mom) and the list is yours to change.
 Off by default: without Seca Link, the app does not use the Internet.
 SMS 
 MMS, both ways. A picture message sent to you arrives and is shown in the conversation. Sending one works too, through your carrier, so it reaches any phone: a picture, a video, a file, a contact card or a voice message, with no account at either end. Pictures are shrunk to what a network will carry. Group conversations over MMS are still being worked on.
 Conversations with your contacts' photos and profiles, search across every message.
 Reply from the notification, scheduled messages.
 Verification codes copied in one tap and erased automatically after a while.
 Advertising texts filed as spam.
 Pinned and archived conversations.
 Also 
 Password-encrypted backup.
 App lock, and a hidden preview in recent apps.
 Wallpaper colours or Seca palettes, dark theme.
No ads, no trackers, no account. Open source.

fdroid:org.schabi.newpipe.localserver.description:
LocalTube is an enhanced, self-hosted streaming server solution built on top of a specialized fork of NewPipe Extractor. By bundling a lightweight and concurrent Java HTTP server inside an Android application, LocalTube enables you to browse, search, and stream content from major streaming platforms directly from any device in your local network using a standard web browser.
Key Features:
- Decentralized Local Server: Runs a lightweight, concurrent Java HTTP server directly on your Android device (default port 8080), serving a modern, responsive web interface.
- Cross-Device Playback: Connect seamlessly to the server from any device on your local network (PC, laptop, smart TV, tablet) by visiting your device's local IP.
- Video.js Media Player: High-performance HTML5 player using Video.js for quality switching, adaptive playback speed, gesture controls, and smooth seeking.
- Enhanced Gestures & Shortcuts: Double-tap or double-click to seek 10s forward/backward (with chevron ripples), swipe vertically to adjust volume (with volume HUD), and use keyboard/remote D-pad shortcuts (Space, J, L, M, Arrows).
- Autoplay Queue: Seamless "Up Next" autoplay timer countdown at the end of video playback with Cancel and Play Now actions.
- Picture-in-Picture & Subtitles: Native floating Picture-in-Picture window support, and fully fixed WebVTT captions/subtitles rendering.
- Remote Playback Control: Remotely control other active clients on your network (play, pause, fast-forward, rewind) from the web interface.
- Database Backup Import/Export: Back up and restore your settings and SQLite watch history as JSON files.
- YouTube Interests & Subscriptions Importer: Log in securely via WebView to scrape and import subscription lists, as well as personalize followed interest keywords using unique homepage recommendation tags.
- Dedicated Reels Player Integration: Open YouTube Reels directly in a specialized vertical scrolling Reels player (supporting swipe controls) from your Watch Later, History, or Search feeds.
- Custom Quality Preferences: Easily manage preferred video streaming resolutions directly inside the client and server settings.
- Theme Customization: Toggle between modern Dark, Light, and Pure Black (OLED) themes with custom accent color palette selection.
- Material 3 User Interface: Beautifully updated UI with cohesive Material Design 3 tokens, color harmonies, and responsive layouts.
- Private Watch History: Tracks your watched videos locally on the host device using a secure SQLite database, maintaining privacy with zero external telemetry or tracking.

fdroid:org.sherpr.app.name: Sherpr
fdroid:org.sherpr.app.summary: Drive your Herdr AI-agent fleet from your phone, over SSH — no cloud
fdroid:org.sherpr.app.description:
Sherpr is the mobile companion for Herdr , the terminal agent multiplexer. Herdr runs each coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, …) in its own real terminal and shows at a glance who is blocked , working , done , or idle . Sherpr brings that glance — and the ability to unblock, steer, and monitor agents — to your pocket.
 What it does 
 Connect securely to a Herdr instance on your workstation, homelab box, or VPS — over SSH, with pinned host keys and on-device Ed25519 keys.
 Fleet dashboard — a live overview of every workspace, tab, and pane with Herdr's semantic status colors, sorted so what needs you floats to the top.

flathub:io.github.heidefinnischen.cuneo.name: Cuneo
flathub:io.github.heidefinnischen.cuneo.description:
Cuneo is a simple and straightforward app that lets you calculate and convert anything you might encounter in your daily life. Being designed like a widget, Cuneo gets out of the way and is best used floating over a maximized window so you can focus on your actual tasks and not managing a calculation app covering half your screen.
 Cuneo's name is inspired by the ancient writing system cuneiform. It is the earliest known wiritng system that's been originally used by the Sumer civilization. One use case for cuneiform was on numerical tablets likely to keep track of taxes, inventory, calculations and many other things people encountered in their daily lives. This is what Cuneo basically is. Cuneo is meant to be used "on-site". For when you need to get something done or look something up really quick. Designed like a tool that lives in your pocket which you get out when you need to crunch some numbers or conversions. 
 Cuneo features two distinct modes: a regular calculation mode and a conversion mode. To help you stay focused and avoid wasting any of your precious screen space, Cuneo skips the usual skeuomorphic calculator buttons. You just use the numbers on your keyboard, they're right there after all. For anything a little more complicated than your keyboard can handle theres an operator menu right at your disposal. Power users can also just type the operators like "sqrt()" for square root. 
 Conversion mode is a powerful conversion multi-tool that offers many different units to convert to and from. Unit types range from Area to Volume and Units inside these categories are grouped by common affiliation like metric and imperial. 
 For both modes Cuneo offers a history window that displays previous entries of your current session.

 CommonMark and GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM), along with other useful notetaking features such

 The documentation can be accessed by opening the demo vault that is shipped in Obsidian.

 or license is required for qualifying use cases described in the End User License Agreement. Users

 your notes. Details about these optional hosted services can be found on the Obsidian website.
 This distribution is verified by the Obsidian team but isn't supported

 Pdflatex support in pandoc currently requires installing the org.freedesktop.Sdk.Extension.texlive
 SDK
 Note: Regular users should disable "Automatic Updates" within Obsidian as public release updates
 are handled by Flatpak itself. Insiders should keep this enabled to receive insider builds, as
 those will not be made available on Flathub.
 This flatpak goes into great lengths to provide a nice experience for end users. In order for
 the Git plugin to work it requires permission to the ssh-auth socket (--socket=ssh-auth). It also
 exposes the home directory in the sandbox (required for Drag and Drop operations). If you don't
 use the Git plugin you can disable the ssh-auth socket permission, e.g. using Flatseal. You can
 also remove access to the home directory if you want and the flatpak will continue to work, albeit
 with reduced functionality. In case you do remove access to the homedir, note that in order for
 things to not break for the Git plugin, --persist=.ssh flag has been passed and a bind mount to
 ~/.var/app/md.obsidian.Obsidian/ is created by flatpak, allowing that location to be used for persistent
 data (but your home directory's .ssh remains unaccessible)

MeBoard is the keyboard you set up your way: glide typing, tunable haptics, any layout you like and a split keyboard for big screens.
GLIDE TYPING
Slide through a word's letters without lifting your finger. MeBoard picks the word using the word before it, adds the space for you and shows other guesses above the keys. Words you use often glide too.
HAPTICS YOU CAN TUNE
Set the strength and feel of every keypress, with a separate feel for letters and for keys like delete and shift. Choose what vibrates: keys, long-presses, even each step as you slide the cursor. Key sounds are optional.
SPLIT KEYBOARD FOR FOLDABLES AND IPAD
On large screens like the iPhone Duo unfolded or an iPad, MeBoard splits into two thumb halves with one wide space bar. Set portrait and landscape separately and choose the gap.
LAYOUTS YOUR WAY
QWERTY, QWERTZ, AZERTY, Dvorak, Colemak, Colemak-DH and Workman, or build your own: add and remove keys, change what they type and their labels, resize them and set long-press characters. Add a number row, adjust height, spacing, corner radius and label size, or switch to one-handed mode.
FAMILIAR IF YOU PREFER
Keep the comma and period beside the space bar, or hide them for a classic iPhone bottom row. Choose symbol pages laid out like Gboard or like the iPhone keyboard.
A TOOLBAR YOU ARRANGE
Show only the buttons you want (hide keyboard, layouts, number row, one-handed, cursor arrows) and put them in any order.
SMART TYPING
• Autocorrect that understands neighboring keys, so "thw" becomes "the", and fixes missing spaces and apostrophes
• Context-aware fixes like "I'm jot" → "I'm not"
• Backspace undoes a correction; tap your original word to keep it
• Next-word predictions that learn your phrases
• Emoji suggestions as you type, like a pizza for "pizza"
• Your own text shortcuts, like "omw" → "On my way!"
• Long-press any key for symbols and accents
• Slide on the space bar to move the cursor; swipe left from delete to erase whole words
• Number pad in number fields, @ in email fields, .com in web addresses
• Light, dark or automatic theme
PRIVATE BY DESIGN
MeBoard has no network code, no analytics and no ads. What you type, the words it learns and your settings never leave your device.
Full Access is only needed for haptics, to load the settings you choose in the app and to remember the words you teach it. MeBoard works without it.

firefox-addons:3003482.name: Hawk Translate
firefox-addons:3003482.summary: More than just a translator: improve your vocabulary, reading, and listening skills in any language using natural-voice pronunciation and word family discovery. With a clean UI and multiple free backends.
firefox-addons:3003482.description:
Hawk Translate is a fast, distraction-free translation and language-learning companion. Select any text on any website to get an instant translation, natural-voice pronunciation, and — for single words — grammar and synonyms to grow your vocabulary. Watch YouTube, Netflix, and Prime Video with two subtitle languages at once, and train your ear with dictation on real lines from the video. Save the words you want to keep and learn them with built-in flash cards.
What you can do
Watch YouTube, Netflix, and Prime Video with bilingual subtitles. A new button in the player shows two subtitle lines at once — the video's language on top, yours below. On YouTube, both lines come from YouTube's own captions (including YouTube's auto-translations) and stay in sync line for line. On Netflix and Prime Video, pair two of the title's own subtitle languages (perfect timing, nothing leaves the page), machine-translate the original track into your language with the provider of your choice, or load your own subtitle file (.srt, .vtt, .ttml) for titles that only ship one language. Machine-translated lines appear progressively and are cached per title, so re-watching never re-translates. On ad-supported Prime streams, subtitles stay in sync across ad breaks. Lines can be resized on the spot, and your language pair is remembered and applies automatically on the next video. Pause and select any subtitle word to translate or ☆-save it — subtitles become study material. If YouTube's auto-translation is unavailable, your translation provider fills in the second line instead.
Practice dictation. On YouTube and Prime Video, turn on bilingual subtitles and choose Dictation practice in the subtitle menu. Hawk hides the subtitles, plays one line from the video, and pauses so you can type what you heard. Every word is marked correct, wrong, missing, or extra, and you get a score plus the line's translation. Replay the line as often as you like, or replay it slower. Pick your level: Beginner uses short lines (6 words or fewer) with half the words already filled in, so you type only the blanks; Intermediate uses lines of up to 12 words; Advanced uses every line. Ask for a hint, skip a line, or show the answer. The practice panel can be dragged anywhere on the video, its text size is adjustable, and you can assign a keyboard shortcut to start and stop it.
Select and translate. Highlight text; a compact bubble shows the translation right next to your selection.
Listen. Click the speaker 🔊 to hear the original or the translation in a natural voice. Click the same text twice for a slower replay — great for pronunciation practice.
Learn vocabulary. Select a single word and Hawk shows its part of speech (noun / verb / adjective …) and synonyms, so you see the whole word family at a glance.
Save words and review them as flash cards. Tap the ☆ on any translation to add it to your study list. Review your words on a spaced-repetition schedule: words you know come back less and less often, words you miss come right back, and words you've mastered graduate out of the rotation. Export your list to Anki, CSV, or JSON anytime.
Keep a local history. Every translation is saved on your device — searchable, filterable by site and date, and exportable. You decide how long it's kept, or turn it off entirely.
Full-text popup. Click the toolbar icon to type or paste anything, pick your target language, and translate.
Right-click menu. Translate any selection from the context menu — no long mouse trips.
Keyboard shortcut. Assign a hotkey to translate the current selection instantly, even on pages where you've turned the bubble off.
Translate PDFs. Opt in to open web PDFs in the bundled viewer, so select-to-translate works on PDF pages just like regular web pages.
Multiple translation backends — no key required
Hawk Translate works out of the box with no setup. Pick your preferred service in the options:
Google — free, default, fast, high quality
MyMemory — free, no key, ~5,000 words per day
DeepL — your own key (free or paid plan)
Microsoft Azure Translator — your own free key (2M characters/month)
LibreTranslate — open source; point it at your own endpoint
If the chosen backend fails, a built-in "Try with …" chooser retries instantly with another provider — no detour through the settings.
Built for language learners
Bilingual subtitles on YouTube, Netflix, and Prime Video turn any captioned video into listening practice: hear the original, read both languages, and save the words you don't know without leaving the player.
Dictation turns watching into active listening: you hear real speakers at natural speed, type what you caught, and see exactly which words you missed. Beginner mode keeps it short and gives you half the words, so you can start without getting frustrated.
A speaker on both the original and the translation lets you hear the source language while you read the meaning.
The word-families panel shows nuance: seeing synonyms grouped by part of speech builds vocabulary faster than a bare translation.
Flash-card review turns the words you actually encountered while browsing into long-term vocabulary — no separate app, no account.
A compact, focused interface that stays out of your way.
Your settings
Theme: Auto / Light / Dark for the popup and the bubble.
Bubble style: Classic (compact) or Card (original and translation, each with its own speaker).
Auto-close: the bubble dismisses itself after a few seconds — hover to pause. Configurable from 0 (off) to 120 seconds.
When the bubble appears: a small hawk icon to click, instantly on selection, or only via popup / right-click.
Per-site control: disable the bubble on sites where you don't want it, straight from the right-click menu.
Supported languages
50+ translation languages, including English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Japanese, Korean, Chinese (Simplified & Traditional), Arabic, Hindi, Vietnamese, Thai, Turkish, Indonesian, Ukrainian, Polish, Dutch, and more. Extension metadata localized in 20 languages.
Privacy
Hawk Translate does not collect or transmit any personal data to the developer. The text you translate is sent only to the provider you choose (Google, MyMemory, DeepL, Azure, or LibreTranslate). Bilingual subtitles read the captions YouTube, Netflix, or Prime Video already serves for the video you're watching; when both lines come from the video's own subtitle tracks, no translation provider is involved and that data never leaves your browser. Dictation practice runs entirely in your browser: it replays the video you're already watching and checks your typing on your device, and your answers are never sent anywhere or saved. If you choose the machine-translate option on Netflix or Prime Video, the subtitle text is sent to the translation provider you picked — just like any other translation — and the result is cached only on your device. On YouTube, if YouTube refuses its auto-translation, the second line is translated by the provider you picked instead: that video's subtitle text is sent to that provider, and the result is cached only on your device. Your translation history, saved words, and flash-card progress are stored only on your device — never uploaded, never synced, and removed if you uninstall. API keys you enter for DeepL, Azure, or LibreTranslate are stored locally in your browser and never sent anywhere except that provider's own servers for requests you trigger.
Open source
MIT licensed.
Hawk Translate is an independent project and is not affiliated with Google, Microsoft, DeepL, or MyMemory.

THE TOOLBOX

BUILT FOR iPad
